item.title: Mind2Report: Expert-Level Commercial Report Synthesis via Cognitive Deep Research Agent
item.description: Synthesizing informative commercial reports from massive and noisy web sources is critical for high-stakes business decisions. Although recent deep research agents (DRAs) achieve notable progress, their reports remain limited in quality, reliability, and coverage. These mainly stem from ambiguous intents that cause search drift, retrieved web content that rapidly saturates the context window, and single-pass synthesis that limits report comprehensiveness. item.title: Persistent memory through triple-loop consolidation under stochastic unit turnover
item.description: Dissipative cognitive architectures maintain computation through continuous energy expenditure, where units that exhaust their energy are stochastically replaced with fresh random state. item.title: TabClaw: An Interactive and Self-Evolving Agent for Spreadsheet Manipulation and Table Reasoning
item.description: Spreadsheets and tables are widely used representations for structured data analysis, but effective analysis still requires substantial manual effort and domain expertise. item.title: LPT: Orchestrating bounded agentic loops for automated protein binder design
item.description: Current large language models (LLMs) can reason over scientific information and use code-based tools, but their training knowledge is broad rather than specialized, can be out of date and is hard to attribute to sources. Furthermore, unconstrained agentic workflows and unlimited tool use can consume large amounts of tokens. item.description: Recursive language models (RLMs) showed that recursion over model calls is an effective strategy for long-context reasoning, and production coding agents have begun to write code that spawns subagents at scale, most recently in Anthropic's dynamic workflows. item.description: Recent search agents for multi-hop reasoning often fail by either retrieving incomplete evidence or reasoning over irrelevant portions of the retrieved content, leading to a retrieval-reasoning boundary shift. item.title: MOSAIC: Unveiling the Moral, Social and Individual Dimensions of Large Language Models
item.description: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed in sensitive applications including psychological support, healthcare, and high-stakes decision-making. item.title: Persona Conditioning as an Assessor-Sensitivity Probe for LLM-Based IR Evaluation
item.description: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used as relevance assessors in information retrieval (IR) evaluation, raising questions about how assessor framing affects judgment reliability and downstream system comparison. item.description: Recent advances in large language models have enabled a new class of agentic data science systems that allow users to complete complex data science workflows through natural language.
